title: Full root towers and punctures commute with profinite and ring base change
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $R$ a commutative ring, $r\geq0$ and $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in R$. Write
$$A_p(R,t)=\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R[x_{d,n}]_{1\leq d\leq r}/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)_d,\qquad T_R=\operatorname{Spec}A_p(R,t),$$
with positive integers prime to $p$ ordered by divisibility and transitions $x_{d,n}\mapsto x_{d,m}^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$ [def-sfb-full-parameter-root-tower]. For every ring map $f:R\to S$ there is a canonical $S$-algebra isomorphism
$$S\otimes_R A_p(R,t)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_p(S,f(t)),$$
sending $s\otimes1$ to $s$ and $1\otimes x_{d,n}$ to $x_{d,n}$. It identifies the base-changed principal open $T_R[1/\prod_{a\in I}t_a]\times_R S$ with $T_S[1/\prod_{a\in I}f(t_a)]$ for every $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$, and is compatible with identity and composite base changes.
For profinite sets $P,Q$, use $X[P]=\operatorname{Spec}LC(P,\mathbf Z)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects], with maps induced by pullback of locally constant integer functions [def-sfb-profinite-product-maps]. Set $R_P=R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}LC(P,\mathbf Z)$. Then $U[P]=\operatorname{Spec}R_P\to U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is affine pro-etale [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; the preceding isomorphism identifies $T_R[P]$ and its indicated opens with the full root tower and the same principal opens over $R_P$. There is also a canonical $(X[P])[Q]\cong X[P\times Q]$ for every affine scheme $X$. All these scheme isomorphisms commute with maps of profinite parameters, ring base change, and their projections to the original schemes. Zero rings, empty parameter sets, $r=0$ and $I=\varnothing$ are included.

proof.text: Use the existing compatible-root presentation A_p(R,t): the polynomial ring in every labelled root, modulo the ideal generated by the power and divisibility relations. Coefficient change maps each relation to the corresponding relation over S, hence descends to a ring map. Surjectivity of the quotient and polynomial ring extensionality show that any map from this quotient is determined by its coefficients and all labelled roots. This works directly with the presentation; no categorical colimit construction is needed.

source.place: Tags 00AR (section-rings-basic) and 00F2 (finite type polynomial presentations); Categories Tag 002F (colimit universal property); explicit evaluation argument by Q57

proof.text: The family of roots in $A_p(S,f(t))$ defines $a_f:A_p(R,t)\to A_p(S,f(t))$, carrying coefficients by $f$ and preserving the labels. The tensor pushout property gives $\Phi_f:S\otimes_R A_p(R,t)\to A_p(S,f(t))$, $s\otimes a\mapsto s\,a_f(a)$. Conversely the elements $1\otimes x_{d,n}$ satisfy $(1\otimes x_{d,n})^n=f(t_d)\otimes1$ and $(1\otimes x_{d,m})^{m/n}=1\otimes x_{d,n}$. Step 1 over $S$ therefore gives $\Psi_f:A_p(S,f(t))\to S\otimes_R A_p(R,t)$ fixing $S$ and sending each labelled root to $1\otimes x_{d,n}$. The composite $\Phi_f\Psi_f$ fixes coefficients and roots, so is the identity by step 1. The other composite fixes $S\otimes1$ and $1\otimes A_p(R,t)$, hence is the identity by uniqueness in the tensor pushout property. These are the claimed inverse $S$-algebra maps.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), tensor pushout formula; explicit compatible-root specialization by Q57

proof.text: For $R\xrightarrow f S\xrightarrow g V$, the maps $a_{gf}$ and $a_g a_f$ agree on coefficients and every labelled root, so are equal by step 1; $a_{\mathrm{id}}$ is the identity for the same reason. The canonical associativity map $V\otimes_S(S\otimes_R A)\to V\otimes_R A$ is $(v\otimes(s\otimes a))\mapsto vg(s)\otimes a$, with inverse $v\otimes a\mapsto v\otimes(1\otimes a)$: balancing verifies both formulas. The composite of the two base-change comparisons sends this generator to $vg(s)a_{gf}(a)$, just as $\Phi_{gf}$ does. Tensor uniqueness proves compatibility with composites and with the unit identifications.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), uniqueness in the tensor formula

proof.text: Apply the affine fibre-product formula to step 2. It gives $T_R\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}S\cong T_S$, and its projections are induced by the coefficient and root maps already specified. Put $h=\prod_{a\in I}t_a$. By the basic-open pullback lemma the inverse image of $D(h)\subset T_R$ under the base-change projection is $D(h\otimes1)$. The comparison identifies this section with $\prod_{a\in I}f(t_a)$, so its restriction is precisely the required isomorphism of open subschemes. Here the pullback of an open subscheme is its inverse-image open with the restricted structure sheaf, directly by the universal property of restriction. This proves the puncture clause as a scheme isomorphism, not only on point sets.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); Modules Tag 0H78 (remark-pullback-s-open) for the inverse-image basic open

proof.text: Put L_P=LC(P,Z) and R_P=R tensor_Z L_P. Construct the tensor pushout by its universal property, using ULift Z as the base ring to respect the universe of the scheme category. Applying Spec gives a pullback square with projections induced by R and L_P. Thus Spec R_P is canonically the profinite product of Spec R with P. Its projection is affine because it is a base change of an affine morphism, and weakly etale by base change of the existing locally constant test object. Paste this pullback square with the root-algebra base-change square of step 4; the pasted square identifies the root tower over R_P with T_R[P]. Inverse-image principal opens restrict this isomorphism, including the structure sheaf and the stated immersion equation.

source.place: Tag 097D (lemma-construct-profinite), finite-quotient construction; More on Morphisms Tag 094U (lemma-base-change-weakly-etale); Schemes Tag 01I4; Morphisms Tag 01SH

proof.text: The functor from profinite sets to pro-etale objects over Spec Z preserves finite limits. Compose it with the forgetful functor to the over category of schemes, then pull back to X. These functors preserve finite limits. The image of the binary product cone therefore exhibits X[P times Q] as the pullback of X[P] and X[Q] over X. Independently, paste the defining scheme pullback squares to show that (X[P])[Q], with its two stated projections, is the same pullback. The unique isomorphism between these pullback cones gives the comparison and both projection equations. All these constructions work for any X; in particular they give the required affine case.

source.place: Statement: preservation of finite limits; explicit application to the binary product, followed by fibre-product reassociation

proof.text: A continuous map $b:P'\to P$ acts on functions by $l\mapsto l\circ b$. In the formulas of step 5 both orders therefore send $(r\otimes l)\otimes a$ to $(l\circ b)\otimes ra$; ring base change likewise replaces $r$ by its image and preserves every labelled root. Tensor uniqueness and step 1 prove all mixed ring/parameter squares commute. Restricting these commuting maps to the inverse-image opens of step 4 preserves these equalities. In step 6 the product comparison commutes with parameter maps because both composites have the same two profinite projections, and reassociation commutes with any scheme map because both composites have the same three projections. These uniqueness checks also show compatibility with every projection to the original schemes. For $r=0$ step 1 has the unique empty family, so the tower algebra is $R$. For $I=\varnothing$, $h=1$ and the open is the entire scheme. For $P=\varnothing$ or $Q=\varnothing$, $LC(\varnothing,\mathbf Z)$ is the zero ring and the corresponding schemes and products are empty. If $R$ or $S$ is zero the same formulas still define mutually inverse maps; no step used injectivity, nonzeroness, invertibility of $p$, or any normality hypothesis.
